questions.q: If two tangents drawn from the point $(h, k)$ to the parabola $y^2=64 x$ be such that the slope of one tangent is 8 times of the other, then the value of $\frac{k^2}{2 h}$ is
questions.solution:
Let the equation of tangent is
$y=m x+\frac{16}{m} [\because a=16]$
It passes through $(h, k)$
Then, $k=m h+\frac{16}{m} \Rightarrow m^2 h+16-m k=0$
According to the question, roots of the equation will be $m_1$ and $8 m_1$.
So, $m_1+8 m_1=\frac{k}{h} \Rightarrow 9 m_1=\frac{k}{h}...(i)$
and $m_1 \cdot 8 m_1=\frac{16}{h} \Rightarrow 8 m_1^2=\frac{16}{h}...(ii)$
By solving these equations, we get
$\frac{k^2}{2 h}=81$

questions.q: The coordinates of the point on the parabola $y=x^2+7 x+2$, which is nearest to the straight line $y=3 x-3$, are
questions.solution:
Any point on the parabola is $\left(x, x^2+7 x+2\right)$
Its distance from the line $y=3 x-3$ is given by
$\begin{aligned} p & =\left|\frac{3 x-\left(x^2+7 x+2\right)-3}{\sqrt{9+1}}\right| \\ & =\left|\frac{x^2+4 x+5}{\sqrt{10}}\right|\end{aligned}=\frac{x^2+4 x+5}{\sqrt{10}}\left[\right.$ as $\left.x^2+4 x+5\gt0, \forall x \in R\right]\begin{aligned} & \therefore & \frac{d p}{d x} & =0 \\ \Rightarrow & & x & =-2\end{aligned}$
So, the required point is $(-2,-8)$.

questions.q: The curve described parametrically by $x=t^2+t+1, y=t^2-t+1$ represents
questions.solution:
We have, $\quad x=t^2+t+1\qquad \mathrm{...(i)}$ and $\quad y=t^2-t+1\qquad \mathrm{...(ii)}$
Now, $\quad x+y=2\left(1+t^2\right)\qquad \mathrm{...(iii)}$ and $\quad x-y=2 t\qquad \mathrm{...(iv)}$
Now, from Eqs. (iii) and (iv), we get
$\begin{aligned}
& x+y=2\left[1+\left(\frac{x-y}{2}\right)^2\right] \\
\Rightarrow & x+y=2\left[\frac{4+x^2+y^2-2 x y}{4}\right] \\
\Rightarrow & x^2+y^2-2 x y-2 x-2 y+4=0 \qquad \mathrm{...(v)}
\end{aligned}\therefore$ On comparing with
$a x^2+2 h x y+b y^2+2 g x+2 f y+c=0$
We get, $a=1, b=1, c=4, h=-1, g=-1$, $f=-1\because \quad \Delta=a b c+2 f g h-a f^2-b g^2-c h^2$
Now, $\quad \Delta=1 \cdot 1 \cdot 4+2(-1)(-1)(-1)-1 \times(-1)^2\begin{aligned}
& -1 \times(-1)^2-4(-1)^2 \\
& =4-2-1-1-4 \\
& =-4 \text{ therefore, } \Delta \neq 0
\end{aligned}$ and $a b-h^2=1 \cdot 1-(1)^2=1-1=0$
So, it is equation of a parabola.

questions.q: Minimum distance between the curves $y^2=4 x$ and $x^2+y^2-12 x+31=0$ is
questions.solution:
Centre and radius of the given circle is P(6,0) and $\sqrt{5}$, respectively.
Now minimum distance between two curves always occurs along a line which normal to both the curves.
Equation of normal to $y^2=4 x$ at $\left(t^2, 2 t\right)$ is
$y=-t x+2 t+t^3$
If it is normal to circle also, then it must pass though $(6,0)$.
$\therefore 0=t^3-4 t \Rightarrow t=0 \quad$ or $t= \pm 2$.
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow A(4,4) \text{$ and $} C(4,-4) \\ & \Rightarrow P A=P C=\sqrt{20}=2 \sqrt{5} . \\ & \Rightarrow \text{ Required minimum distance }=2 \sqrt{5}-\sqrt{5}=\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The mid-point of the line joining the common points of the line $2 x-3 y+8=0$ and $y^2=8 x$ is
questions.solution:
Let $\left(x_1, y_1\right)$ be the mid-point of the line joining the common points of the given line and the given parabola. Then, the equation of line is
$\begin{aligned}
& y y_1-4\left(x+x_1\right)=y_1^2-8 x_1 \\
\Rightarrow & 4 x-y y_1+y_1^2-4 x_1=0
\end{aligned}$
This line and $2 x-3 y+8=0$ represents the same line.
$\begin{array}{ll}
\therefore & \frac{4}{2}=\frac{-y_1}{-3}$=$\frac{y_1^2-4 x_1}{8}$ \\
\Rightarrow & y_1=6, y_1^2-4 x_1=16 \\
\Rightarrow & y_1=6, x_1=$\frac{36-16}{4} \\
\Rightarrow & y_1=6, x_1=5
\end{array}$\therefore$ The required point is $(5,6)$.$

questions.q: If the normal to the parabola $y^2=4 a x$ at the point $\left(a t^2, 2 a t\right)$ cuts the parabola again at $\left(a T^2, 2 a T\right)$, then
questions.solution:
Equation of the normal of the parabola $y^2=4 a x$ at the point $\left(a t^2, 2 a t\right)$ is $y+t x=2 a t+a t^3...(i)\because$ Eq. (i) cuts the parabola again at $\left(a T^2, 2 a T\right)$.
Then, $2 a T+t a T^2=2 a t+a t^3\Rightarrow \quad 2 a(T-t)=-a t\left(T^2-t^2\right)\Rightarrow \quad 2=-t(T+t) \quad(\because t \neq T)\Rightarrow \quad t^2+t T+2=0\because t$ is real, $\therefore T^2-4 \cdot 1 \cdot 2 \geq 0\Rightarrow \quad T^2 \geq 8$

questions.solution:
The equation of parabola whose vertex is $(-1,-2)$ is
$(x+1)^2=4 a(y+2)$
which passes through $(3,6)$
i.e. $16=4 a \times 8 \Rightarrow a=\frac{1}{2}\therefore$ Required equation is
$(x+1)^2=2(y+2) \text{ or } x^2+2 x-2 y-3=0$

questions.solution:
Given equation of parabola is $y^2=4 a x$. Let the co-ordinates of $B$ are ( $a t^2, 2 a t$ ), then the slope of $A B=\frac{2}{t}$
Since, $B C \perp A B\therefore$ Slope of $B C=\frac{-t}{2}$ The equation of $B C$ is $y-2=-\frac{t}{2}\left(x-a t^2\right)\because$ This line meets the $X$-axis at point $O$ So, put $y=0$, we get $\Rightarrow \quad x=4 a+a t^2$
So, the distance $C D=4 a+a t^2-a t^2=4 a$

questions.q: The equation of the common tangent to the curves $y^2=8 x$ and $x y=-1$ is
questions.solution:
Tangent to the curve $y^2=8 x$ is $y=m x+\frac{2}{m}$.
So, it must satisfy $x y=-1\Rightarrow x\left(m x+\frac{2}{m}\right)=-1 \Rightarrow m x^2+\frac{2}{m} x+1=0$
Since, it has equal roots.
$\therefore \quad D=0\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow & \frac{4}{m^2}-4 m=0 \\
\Rightarrow & m^3=1 \Rightarrow m=1
\end{array}$ \\ So, equation of common tangent is $y=x+2$.

questions.q: If the line $y-\sqrt{3} x+3=0$ cuts the parabola $y^2=x+2$ at $A$ and $B$, then $P A \cdot P B$ is equal to where [where $P=(\sqrt{3}, 0)]$.
questions.solution:
Given $P=(\sqrt{3}, 0)\therefore$ Equation of line A B$ is
\frac{x-\sqrt{3}}{\cos 60^{{}^{\circ}}}=\frac{y-0}{\sin 60^{{}^{\circ}}}=r \begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad x=\sqrt{3}+\frac{r}{2}, y=\frac{r \sqrt{3}}{2} \\
& \therefore \text{ point }\left(\sqrt{3}+\frac{r}{2}, \frac{r \sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \text{ lies on } y^2=x+2 \\
& \therefore \\
& \Rightarrow \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{3 r^2}{4}=\sqrt{3}+\frac{r}{2}+2 \\
& \Rightarrow-\frac{r}{2}-(2+\sqrt{3})=0
\end{aligned}$Let the roots be $r_1 and r_2$, then the product
$\begin{aligned}
r_1 \times r_2 & =P A \cdot P B=\left|\frac{-(2+\sqrt{3})}{\frac{3}{4}}\right| \\
& =\frac{4(2+\sqrt{3})}{3}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two common tangents to the circle $x^2+y^2=2 a^2$ and parabola $y^2=8 a x$ are
questions.solution:
The equation of any tangent to $y^2=8 a x$ is
$y=m x+\frac{2 a}{m}$  ...(i)
If it touches $x^2+y^2=2 a^2$, then
$\left(\frac{2 a}{m}\right)^2=2 a^2\left(1+m^2\right)\left[\because c^2=a^2\left(1+m^2\right)\right]\Rightarrow \quad 2=m^2\left(m^2+1\right)\begin{array}{rlrl}\Rightarrow & m^4+m^2-2 & =0 \\ \Rightarrow & \left(m^2+2\right) \left(m^2-1\right)$ & =0 \\ \Rightarrow & & m^2-1 & =0 \\ \Rightarrow & & m & = \pm 1\end{array}$
Putting the values of $m$ in Eq. (i), we get $y= \pm(x+2 a)$ as the equations of common tangents.$
